name: One match with its replay
description: Two rows out of Postgres: replay_key for the presign task, and one `body` column holding the whole response. The seats come from match_seats -- under v2 a match's players are rows, not three positionally-aligned arrays -- so this is an ordinary join and `seat` is the column rather than an ordinality. `rating_change` is a second join onto rating_events, which is null until count has folded the match: that is the point of showing status alongside it, because a competitor sees the result before they see what it did to their rating. A cancelled match carries withdrawn_reason and, where a promotion caused it, the successor that replaced the seat; a failed one carries the fault and which seat it was attributed to. replay_url is null for any row that never produced a replay.

input.query: SELECT mt.replay_key, json_build_object( 'id', mt.id, 'game', g.slug, 'status', mt.status, 'seed', mt.seed, 'preset', mt.preset, 'reason', mt.reason, 'turns', mt.turns, 'played_ms', mt.played_ms, 'played_at', mt.played_at, 'created_at', mt.created_at, 'withdrawn_reason', mt.withdrawn_reason, 'successor_id', mt.successor_id, 'fault_reason', mt.fault_reason, 'fault_seat', mt.fault_seat, 'engine_digest', mt.engine_digest_played, 'evaluator_digest', mt.evaluator_digest, 'is_trial', mt.trial_model_id IS NOT NULL, 'players', (SELECT coalesce(json_agg(json_build_object( 'seat', s.seat, 'model_id', s.model_id, 'owner', u.handle, 'model_version', md.version, 'rank', s.rank, 'score', s.score, 'strikes', s.strikes, 'rating_change', (SELECT json_object_agg(e.ladder, json_build_object( 'mu_before', e.mu_before, 'sigma_before', e.sigma_before, 'mu_after', e.mu_after, 'sigma_after', e.sigma_after)) FROM rating_events e WHERE e.match_id = mt.id AND e.seat = s.seat)) ORDER BY s.seat), '[]'::json) FROM match_seats s LEFT JOIN models md ON md.id = s.model_id LEFT JOIN users u ON u.id = md.owner_id WHERE s.match_id = mt.id)) AS body FROM matches mt JOIN games g ON g.id = mt.game_id WHERE mt.id = ($1)::uuid
